one_month_reasoning: Two scheduled company events fall inside the window: September sales on Oct 8 and 3Q26 results plus 4Q guidance on Oct 15 (TSMC calendar). July+August revenue was NT$982B, about US$30.7B at the guided 32 NT$/US$, so September only needs about US$14-15B to reach the US$44.6-45.8B guide. August alone was about US$16B, so a beat at or above the top of the range is likely. That is largely expected, though: after the 2Q beat and guidance raise in July the ADR fell after hours (-1.5%) and dropped as low as $372 within the month. The FOMC meets Oct 27-28 (Kalshi: 65% hold, 33% hike, Sep 30), which tilts slightly hawkish. Momentum is positive (stock +10% from its August level, near its high). Net: a small upward drift (median about $463, roughly +0.8%) with the stock's usual monthly vol of 40%/3.5, about 11.4%. I take no strong directional bet because TSM's reaction to earnings beats has been mixed.

fair_value.method: Blend of (a) a 20x forward multiple on NTM EPS of about $24.4/ADR as of Oct 2027 (25% CY27 consensus $21.93 + 75% CY28 estimate $25.2), giving $488, and (b) the 10-year average trailing P/E of about 22x on CY27 EPS of $21.93, giving $482. Weights 0.6/0.4, blended to about $487.

bear.story: AI capex digestion and/or a 2027 US recession (Kalshi ~38% by end-2027) hit a stock trading at a cycle-high multiple. The SOX median drawdown is -35%, and TSM fell about 50% in 2022 and about 33% in 2024-25. Multiple goes to ~15x on about $20 EPS. A Taiwan Strait shock (Polymarket 13% for an invasion by end-2027) is a fatter tail below this.

base.story: EPS compounds about 25-30% into 2027 as N2 ramps and CoWoS stays tight, but the multiple drifts from ~21x toward the 10y average of ~20x. The price tracks earnings, with a return near the history-conditional median (+21% after a >45% trailing year) minus some multiple compression.

bull.story: The AI cycle extends like 2023-24 (a +60-80% follow-on year happened in about 30% of past strong-momentum months). CY28 EPS moves toward $27-28, the stock holds about 25x, and pricing power plus a dividend hike support the re-rating.

thesis_break_reason: $330 is about 28% below today, below the March 2026 low ($314-338 area), and equals about 15x CY27 consensus EPS, the bottom quartile of TSM's 10-year P/E range. Trading there would most likely mean the market sees 2027 earnings going down (AI capex cuts by hyperscalers, a severe Section 232 widening, or a Strait blockade risk), not ordinary 40%-vol noise. A 1-sigma move at 40% vol is about $300-$650 around the median, so this sits at the lower edge.

reasoning: Anchor: from TSM's own 26-year monthly history (308 overlapping 12-month windows, Twelve Data), the unconditional 12-month log return averages +13% with a 31% sd (5th/50th/95th percentiles -35%/+17%/+88%). Conditioned on a trailing 12-month gain above 45% (today +64%), 42 months show a median forward return of +21% and only 62% positive. These cluster into a few episodes (2000 bust -64%; 2010-11, 2021-22 negative; 2020, 2023-24 strongly positive), so the effective sample is small and bimodal. SOX history adds that drawdowns of at least 25% recur every few years (median -35%). Fundamentals support the base case: 2026 growth slightly above 40%, Q2 GM 67.7%, Aug sales +53% YoY, CY27 consensus EPS $21.93 (+30%) with upward revisions. But the trailing P/E (~33x) sits at the top of its 10-year range. My valuation (~$487) implies only modest upside because I assume partial multiple normalisation. Macro and event odds from prediction markets: Kalshi/Polymarket recession by end-2027 at 35-39%, Fed hiking (Sep hike, 33% odds of another in Oct), Polymarket AI-bubble-burst by mid-2027 at 18% (thin volume), and Taiwan invasion by end-2027 at 13% ($3.3M volume; I treat this as an upper bound and use about 5% for a crash component inside the horizon). The ladder is a mixture: 95% lognormal with median $492 and sigma 0.355 (slightly below the 40% realized vol, close to the 3-year monthly vol of 29-36%), plus a 5% crash component with median $210. The result is P(≥ today) 55%, below the 62% historical conditional base rate because of the valuation and the fat left tail. Mean is about $505, close to the scenario mean. The street PT of $552 sits near my 36th percentile. Research went through web search, fetch and Twelve Data; analyst estimate endpoints were paywalled, so consensus EPS comes from secondary aggregators. I did not consult any option data.
